properties.content: Question: common symptoms of lung cancer Answer: Common symptoms of lung cancer include:: - Persistent cough: A cough that lasts for more than three weeks or worsens over time. - Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during exertion. - Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound when breathing. - Chest pain: Pain or discomfort in the chest that may worsen with deep breathing or coughing. - Hoarseness: A change in the voice that makes it sound raspy or low. - Coughing up blood or mucus: Blood or rust-colored mucus may be present in the sputum. - Fatigue: Feeling tired or weak all the time. - Weight loss: Unintentional weight loss without any other obvious reason. - Bone pain: Pain in the bones, especially in the back, hips, or ribs. - Shoulder pain: Pain or weakness in one shoulder. - Headaches: Frequent or severe headaches. - Fever: A fever that does not go away. - Nausea and vomiting: Feeling sick to your stomach or throwing up. - Swelling in the face or neck: Swelling in the face, neck, or lymph nodes. It's important to note that not all people with lung cancer will experience all of these symptoms. Some people may not have any symptoms until the cancer has advanced. If you experience any of these symptoms, it's important to see a doctor promptly for evaluation.
properties.formattedContent:
Question: common symptoms of lung cancer

Answer: 
Common symptoms of lung cancer include::
- Persistent cough: A cough that lasts for more than three weeks or worsens over time.
- Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing, especially during exertion.
- Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound when breathing.
- Chest pain: Pain or discomfort in the chest that may worsen with deep breathing or coughing.
- Hoarseness: A change in the voice that makes it sound raspy or low.
- Coughing up blood or mucus: Blood or rust-colored mucus may be present in the sputum.
- Fatigue: Feeling tired or weak all the time.
- Weight loss: Unintentional weight loss without any other obvious reason.
- Bone pain: Pain in the bones, especially in the back, hips, or ribs.
- Shoulder pain: Pain or weakness in one shoulder.
- Headaches: Frequent or severe headaches.
- Fever: A fever that does not go away.
- Nausea and vomiting: Feeling sick to your stomach or throwing up.
- Swelling in the face or neck: Swelling in the face, neck, or lymph nodes.
It's important to note that not all people with lung cancer will experience all of these symptoms. Some people may not have any symptoms until the cancer has advanced. If you experience any of these symptoms, it's important to see a doctor promptly for evaluation.
